Linear quantile mixed model over a grid of quantiles

Source: R/quant-lqmm.R
wgh_lqmm.Rd

Fits lqmm::lqmm() with a random intercept per child at each quantile, with a retry ladder (more iterations and a looser tolerance, then the derivative-free optimiser) that moves to the next step whenever lqmm reports non-convergence or fails, a convergence log, slopes of the exposure at stated ages by contrast and a child-level cluster bootstrap. Worker functions carry only what they need, which avoids the gigabyte-sized parallel exports documented in the BMI and height-for-age distribution study (Ho 2026, medRxiv 2026.09.08.26362487).

Usage

wgh_lqmm(
  x,
  formula,
  taus = wgh_taus("headline"),
  exposure = "baz",
  anchor_ages = c(6, 9, 12, 15),
  fixed = list(),
  B = wgh_opt("B"),
  iter = wgh_opt("lqmm_iter"),
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

x

Growth data (one sex at a time, or include sex in the formula).

formula

Model formula, for example haz ~ splines::ns(age, knots = c(8, 11, 14), Boundary.knots = c(5, 18)) * baz + site.

taus

Quantiles (rounded with wgh_taus()).

exposure

Exposure whose slope is reported.

anchor_ages

Ages at which slopes are reported.

fixed

Values for other model variables in the slope contrasts (default: first factor level and the mean of numeric variables).

B

Bootstrap replicates (default from the run mode). 0 skips the bootstrap.

iter

Initial LP_max_iter (default from the run mode).

seed

Random seed.

Value

An object of class wgh_lqmm (like wgh_rq, with fits and a convergence table).

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- growdat[growdat$sex == "Male" & growdat$age >= 5, ]
d <- d[d$pid %in% names(which(table(d$pid) >= 3)), ]
f <- haz ~ splines::ns(age, df = 3) * baz
fit <- wgh_lqmm(d, f, taus = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), anchor_ages = c(7, 10, 13), B = 0)
fit$slopes
#> # A tibble: 9 × 3
#>     age   tau estimate
#>   <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1     7  0.25   0.0389
#> 2    10  0.25   0.107 
#> 3    13  0.25   0.119 
#> 4     7  0.5    0.0992
#> 5    10  0.5    0.144 
#> 6    13  0.5    0.143 
#> 7     7  0.75   0.0385
#> 8    10  0.75   0.0843
#> 9    13  0.75   0.0872
# }
